title: Strengthening Resources for Peer Support of Mental Health in Community Settings and Workplaces
what_it_is: Strengthening Resources for Peer Support of Mental Health in Community Settings and Workplaces

sections.label: Peer supporter training programmes
sections.summary: HPB, NCSS, MOM, WSH Council and AIC run peer supporter training, workplace champion and mental health awareness programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Participants are trained to recognise peers in distress, provide active listening and guide them to seek help early.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: From this year onwards, HPB's peer supporter training will be available in a hybrid format and offer additional modules to enhance training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Additionally, the National Council of Social Service's (NCSS') peer support specialist programme trains persons with lived experiences to support others on their recovery journeys.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Council have established the Well-being Champions Network to provide workplace-appointed Champions with the necessary resources and training to better support their organisations in promoting workplace mental health well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) also offers online mental health awareness modules to better equip frontliners to help persons with mental health needs navigate the service landscape.

sections.label: Peer support as scaffold
sections.summary: Peer support is a scaffold for community needs, not meant to carry mental health care that professionals should do.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Ultimately, peer support is meant as a scaffold to support the greater needs of the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: They are not meant to carry the burden of mental health care that the professionals should be doing.

sections.label: Peer support informal scaffold
sections.summary: Peer support is an informal scaffold around formal support and should not be burdened as part of formalised care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As I said in my reply, peer support is meant to be an informal scaffold around formal levels of support and I think we should not put a burden on them to be part of the formalised care structure.

sections.label: Reaching harder to reach persons
sections.summary: With no external manifestation visible, focus is on education and community care teams to reach and encourage those in need.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: There is no external manifestation that you can see from far away.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And so, the focus for us would be to increase education and also to put forth our community care teams, so that those with needs in the community, especially the harder to reach ones, if we know who they are, we can then find a way to reach out to them and encourage them to step forward and seek care.
